Sam: Heads-up — we have a regression on multi-GPU inference perf after the kernel-selector tweak. 8-GPU TP+PP job shows much worse tail latency and reduced throughput in steady-state. Repro on staging.
Maria: Any changes to graphs or stream reuse recently? :thinking_face:
Sam: Yeah, the kernel selector now chooses a different matmul kernel for seq_len 1024 vs 512. Also started reusing CUDA graphs for the hot loop to reduce launch overhead.
Leo: Do you see the all-reduce taking longer or compute stalling?
Sam: Profiling shows NCCL all-reduces look fine in isolation, but compute kernels are serializing around the collectives sometimes. Trying to paste the nsight timeline snippet:

```
# condensed timeline
GPU0: |computeA|computeB|cudaGraphLaunch|computeC|
GPU0:           -----nccl-allreduce (overlaps expected)-----

Observed: computeB waits for allreduce to finish before computeC starts; expected overlap between computeC and the tail of allreduce.
```

Maria: Is this only with graph-launch? Could be stream semantics change inside cudaGraph capture/replay.
Ashley: We had a similar flake when we captured streams that used cudaStreamWaitEvent vs implicit dependencies. If an event is recorded on a stream and replayed in a graph, the replay may serialize differently across devices.
Jia: Also KV-cache prefetch uses a separate stream (kv_stream) and we record events to sync prefetch to compute stream. If graph capture includes those record/wait pairs, they can become host-side dependencies at replay time.
Sam: Exact. When we enable KV prefetch (async) + cudaGraph reuse, the prefetch recordEvent ends up inside the graph and the replay enforces a stricter ordering across streams. That kills comm/compute overlap.
Leo: Can you paste the minimal repro command and the small trace? I want to see if it's reproducible with a single batch.
Sam: repro script: `./tools/run_infer.sh --model gpt-xl --tp 2 --pp 4 --batch 4 --seq 1024 --use-kv-prefetch --cuda-graph`.

DevBot: deploy/ci at 2026-03-15T09:12:01Z — staging build 2026.03.15-2314 finished

Maria: Quick workaround: disable cudaGraph for runs that enable KV prefetch, or make KV prefetch use host-side pinned copy + explicit host synchronization instead of stream events recorded inside graphs.
Ashley: Another fix: ensure prefetch uses the same stream as compute or use cudaGraphLaunch on both streams to keep captured semantics consistent. But that may reduce concurrency.
Jia: We could change to `cudaStreamWaitEvent(compute_stream, kv_event, 0)` outside the graph before replay, i.e., use host-side fence so graph replay doesn't capture the wait. But that adds host synchronization cost.
Sam: I tried a patch where we recordEvent+cudaStreamWaitEvent outside capture; it restores overlap but increases latency variance slightly.
Leo: Could also move NCCL ops to a dedicated comm stream and use `ncclGroupStart/End` there; but NCCL sometimes creates implicit sync with compute if using in-graph calls.
Maria: Important: kernel-selector change altered which kernels run on the compute stream (different occupancy and registers), which changes timing and makes the rare serialization more likely. So it's a timing-sensitive race.
Ashley: Actionable items:
- repro and capture full nsight timeline for patched vs unpatched graph usage (Sam)
- try a variant where KV prefetch is always on compute_stream (Jia)
- try disabling cudaGraph for captured segments that include inter-stream events (Leo)

Sam: I'll attach a minimal nsight capture to the issue. For now rolling back graph reuse for seq_len>=1024 workloads seems safest.
Jia: Filed issue INF-8732 with timeline and repro command. Assigning to eng-runtime. :white_check_mark:
Maria: Nice. Also add a unit perf-test harness that exercises KV prefetch + graphs to catch this early.
Sam: Thanks — I'll open the PR for rollback and include a test. Will ping when CI green.
DevBot: PR #4512 opened by Sam: rollback cudaGraph reuse for seq_len >= 1024 in kernel-selector path — https://git.internal/r/4512
Leo: If someone wants to pair on the nsight trace later I can help interpret the GPU-side stalls.
Sam: Thanks everyone. Keeping this thread updated with trace attachments and perf numbers.
